title: Botany
subtitle: How plants work
summary: Van Helmont grew a willow in a tub for five years. The tree gained 74 kilograms; the soil lost about 60 grams. Where the rest came from is the first lesson, and the course goes on asking that kind of question: how water climbs a hundred metres up a tree with no pump, and how a seedling in the dark knows which way the light is. Branches cover naming plants with a key, crops from maize to Palouse wheat, and a few strange ones that eat insects or warm their own flowers.
